2608.03791.title: Does Forgetting Transfer Across Modalities? A Real-World Benchmark for Cross-Modal Knowledge Unlearning Evaluation
2608.03791.paper_summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs), like Large Language Models (LLMs), may memorize sensitive, copyrighted, or harmful knowledge from their pretraining corpora. Removing such knowledge is essential for building trustworthy AI systems. However, existing studies primarily focus on forgetting within individual modalities. Although recent work has begun to explore cross-modal consistency in unlearning, the cross-modal transfer of real-world knowledge unlearning remains insufficiently studied. To address this gap, we introduce UNLINK-VL, a real-world benchmark for cross-modal knowledge unlearning in VLMs. Under a post-hoc unlearning setting in which the original forget and retain corpora are unavailable, UNLINK-VL selects visually identifiable real-world entities as unlearning targets and associates them with corresponding images and one-hop and multi-hop facts derived from Wikidata. The benchmark comprises four complementary subsets that evaluate direct forgetting of target knowledge, the propagation of forgetting through relational knowledge, the preservation of related non-target knowledge, and robustness to semantically equivalent queries. We train models under text-only and multimodal unlearning settings and evaluate forgetting effectiveness and retained utility across textual, visual, and cross-modal scenarios. Extensive experiments reveal a pronounced asymmetry in cross-modal transfer: multimodal unlearning remains effective under textual evaluation, whereas text-only unlearning transfers poorly to visual and cross-modal scenarios. Meanwhile, the evaluated methods largely preserve the models' general capabilities. These findings demonstrate that relying solely on intra-modal evaluation, particularly text-only evaluation, may substantially overestimate the effectiveness of knowledge unlearning in VLMs, underscoring the need for cross-modal unlearning and evaluation.
2608.03791.paper_summary_zh: 視覺-語言模型（VLMs），如大型語言模型（LLMs），可能會記住其預訓練語料庫中的敏感、受版權保護或有害知識。移除這些知識對於建立值得信賴的人工智慧系統至關重要。然而，現有的研究主要集中在單一模態內的遺忘。儘管最近的工作已開始探索跨模態一致性在遺忘中的應用，但現實世界知識的跨模態遺忘仍然研究不足。為了解決這一空白，我們引入了UNLINK-VL，一個針對VLMs的跨模態知識遺忘的現實世界基準。在一個後驗遺忘的設定中，原始的遺忘和保留語料庫不可用，UNLINK-VL選擇可視識別的現實世界實體作為遺忘目標，並將其與相應的圖像以及來自Wikidata的一跳和多跳事實相關聯。該基準包含四個互補的子集，評估目標知識的直接遺忘、通過關聯知識的遺忘傳播、相關非目標知識的保留，以及對語義等價查詢的穩健性。我們在僅文本和多模態遺忘的設定下訓練模型，並評估在文本、視覺和跨模態場景中的遺忘效果和保留效用。廣泛的實驗揭示了跨模態轉移中的顯著不對稱性：多模態遺忘在文本評估中仍然有效，而僅文本遺忘在視覺和跨模態場景中轉移效果不佳。與此同時，被評估的方法在很大程度上保留了模型的整體能力。這些發現表明，僅依賴模態內評估，特別是僅文本評估，可能會大幅高估VLMs中知識遺忘的有效性，強調了跨模態遺忘和評估的必要性。
